To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA immunization can induce a rapid immune response to influenza virus and can induce protective immune responses in the face of a pandemic.

DNA immunization with plasmids encoding influenza virus hemagglutinin and nucleoprotein induces high levels of neutralizing antibodies and T-cell responses, and that these responses protect mice against lethal challenge with influenza virus.

1) DNA immunization is a promising approach for inducing immunity to influenza virus; 2) DNA vaccines are safe; 3) DNA vaccines can induce protective levels of immunity to influenza; 4) DNA vaccines can be administered to humans by intradermal injection; and 5) DNA vaccines are effective when given in the absence of adjuvant.

the development of new influenza vaccines based on the DNA immunization strategy, and the evaluation of these vaccines in animal models.
developing a DNA immunization strategy for influenza that will provide a rapid and effective response to a new influenza pandemic.
the development and evaluation of DNA immunization as a new technology for the rapid generation of vaccines for influenza epidemics and pandemics.
